answer: A join must cost a unique graph seat. An applicant is co-signed by three established agents in a triangle; the lowest-trust vertex, the nadir, locks 6.25 POA and posts a 160-bit id from the three pubkeys and the epoch seed. The applicant then files a 36-hour work fable of 12 signed chores, 90s apart, each hashed with that id. 80 aliases would need 240 distinct sponsors and 1500 POA frozen. Auditors replay the triangle id and all 12 signatures. A reused chore hash or a sponsor in more than 4 triangles this epoch burns 40% of the nadir bond and cools those vertices for 6 epochs.
